summary: Verified complete removal of KTP/Sunmi/Bluetooth printer SDK integration and the admin Printer settings section. Backend: 4 removed endpoints return 404/405, thermal receipt HTML still works with '@media print' + '@page { size: 58mm' (no 'auto'), a4 format still works. All 7 pytest cases pass. Admin UI: Instellingen sidebar/hub contain NO 'Printers' section (0 occurrences of 'printer' in page body); /admin/instellingen#printers hash gracefully falls back to 'Mijn abonnement' without crash — all other sections (abonnement/bedrijf/branding/smtp/invoicing/kiosk/stripe/backup) still visible. Kiosk web (no APK): after Vooruitbetaling→Contant→Bevestig, exactly 1 hidden iframe 'kiosk-autoprint-iframe' is created and iframe.contentWindow.print() is called once (__printCalls=1); window.__rnMsgs stays null; no requests to /api/kiosk/printer-settings. Kiosk APK (window.ReactNativeWebView mocked): exactly ONE PRINT_RECEIPT postMessage with keys {type,url,data} (no 'printer'/'command'); url ends '/api/payments/<id>/print.html?format=thermal&preview=1'; data has exact 6 keys naam/appartement/bedrag/methode/datum/kwitantie; NO autoprint iframe is created and __printCalls=0. Manual reprint button in APK mode sends one additional PRINT_RECEIPT with the same url.
critical_code_review_comments: Minor: sendApkPrint() in KioskLayout.jsx (~L2400) emits 'console.log([APK PRINT_RECEIPT], msg)' BEFORE the ReactNativeWebView check — so the log fires even in a plain web browser (no RN postMessage happens, just console noise). Harmless, but misleading in dev tools; consider moving the log inside the if-block.

In APK mode the auto-send (PaymentConfirm.sendApkPrint) sends rich data {naam,appartement,bedrag,methode,datum,kwitantie} but the manual reprint path goes through printReceipt() in lib/kiosk-print.js which sends only data:{payment_id}. Both include the url, so the APK can render either way, but the shapes diverge. If the APK relies on the data object for rendering, consider unifying the two senders.

In the thermal preview response, the backend injects a client-side 'page_fit_script' that still runs 'window.print()' inside '<script>'. In an iframe sandbox (as created by the autoprint iframe) scripts are blocked ('Blocked script execution ... sandboxed and allow-scripts not set') — chrome prints a sandbox warning in console. Since the iframe already calls contentWindow.print() from the parent window, this is not a functional problem, but the warning is noisy. Consider adding sandbox='allow-scripts allow-same-origin' on the iframe or skipping the fit-script when preview=1.
Admin Instellingen sections: fallback hash handler (activeInstellingenSection) correctly returns 'abonnement' for unknown hashes like '#printers' — no crash. Good.
